name: Re:amaze
tagline: The GoDaddy-owned ecommerce helpdesk that writes and edits Shopify orders directly inside the chat window, priced to undercut the category's bigger names.
tldr: Re:amaze is a multichannel helpdesk built specifically around ecommerce — email, live chat, SMS/MMS, social media, and voice unified in one inbox, with native Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and Magento integrations at its core.
Founded in 2012 by David Feng, Heng Woon Ong, and Lu Wang, and acquired by GoDaddy in April 2021, where it now operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary.

Pricing is per-user and genuinely affordable relative to category peers: Basic $29/mo, Pro $49/mo, Plus $69/mo (roughly 10% cheaper billed annually), plus a flat-rate $59/mo Starter plan for unlimited team members capped at 500 conversations/month.

The AI Agent is trained on FAQ articles, response templates, custom context, and — distinctively — live Shopify and WooCommerce product and order data, with 5-20 AI resolutions included per user depending on tier and $0.85 for each additional resolution.

The Shopify and WooCommerce integrations go further than most competitors: agents (and the documentation implies, potentially the AI) can create or edit orders directly inside the chat interface, not just view them.

Best for small-to-mid ecommerce brands on Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, or Magento who want deep native commerce data at a lower price point than Gorgias or Gladly — not for teams needing deep Salesforce/HubSpot CRM sync, native multi-language support, or non-WordPress website-builder integrations.
keyFeatures: A knowledge-oriented AI Agent that pulls from FAQ articles, response templates, custom AI context, and live Shopify/WooCommerce product and order data to respond instantly
Native Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and Magento integrations letting agents create or edit orders directly inside the chat interface, not just view them
Pre-built chatbots for FAQs, order-status lookups, and common ecommerce questions, alongside the ability to build custom chatbot flows
A single unified inbox spanning email, live chat, SMS/MMS, social media profiles, and voice
Live visitor view and live screensharing (Peek) on higher tiers for real-time, in-context support
Multi-brand management, department routing, staff performance reporting, and shift/vacation tracking on the Plus tier
Team collaboration tools including staff notes and a built-in 'simple CRM' view of customer conversation history
Broad Zapier connectivity reaching roughly 9,000 other apps, alongside a documented WordPress plugin with a Lightbox Widget

faq.question: Is Re:amaze still an independent company?
faq.answer: No — Re:amaze was acquired by GoDaddy in April 2021 and now operates as a wholly-owned subsidiary. It still runs and markets under its own brand and pricing, but its long-term product direction sits under GoDaddy's ownership rather than an independent founder-led roadmap.

faq.question: How does Re:amaze's AI Agent pricing work?
faq.answer: AI resolutions are included per user per month depending on tier — 5 on Basic, 10 on Pro, 20 on Plus — with each additional resolution beyond that allowance billed at $0.85. This is a comparable per-resolution rate to several competitors (Help Scout's $0.75, Intercom's $0.99), but bundled with a monthly allowance rather than a fully separate metered product.

faq.question: How deep is the Shopify integration, really?
faq.answer: Deeper than most competitors: agents can create or edit Shopify orders directly inside the chat interface, not just view order status in a read-only sidebar. The AI Agent is also documented as pulling from live Shopify (and WooCommerce) product and order data as part of its training context, which is a meaningfully more commerce-aware foundation than a chatbot trained only on static FAQ content.

faq.question: Does Re:amaze integrate with Salesforce or HubSpot?
faq.answer: Not natively in any depth we could confirm. Re:amaze includes a built-in 'simple CRM' — customer profiles and conversation history across channels — but this is positioned as a lighter, conversation-centric alternative to a pipeline-first CRM rather than a Salesforce or HubSpot sync. Teams needing deep CRM integration would likely need to route through Zapier.

faq.question: Does Re:amaze support multiple languages?
faq.answer: Not natively as a built-in feature. We found translation handled through a Zapier integration (Translate by Zapier) rather than an automatic, built-in multi-language or auto-detection capability inside Re:amaze itself — a real gap versus competitors with native translation features.

faq.question: How does Re:amaze compare to Gorgias on price?
faq.answer: Re:amaze is meaningfully cheaper at the entry level — $29/user/month (Basic) or a flat $59/month Starter plan for unlimited team members capped at 500 conversations — against Gorgias's ticket-based pricing that starts at $10/month but scales differently by volume rather than seats. For a small team with several agents and modest ticket volume, Re:amaze's per-user model is often the more predictable and affordable option.

pricingBreakdown: Re:amaze is priced to undercut its closest ecommerce-focused peers meaningfully. A 5-agent team on Basic pays $145/month ($130.50 annual) — well under Gladly's reported enterprise minimums and comparable to or cheaper than Gorgias's mid-tier ticket-based plans for similar volume. The flat-rate $59/month Starter plan is a genuinely distinctive option for a very early-stage business: unlimited team members for one flat price, with the tradeoff being a hard 500-conversation monthly cap rather than a per-seat structure. AI pricing follows the category-standard per-resolution overage model ($0.85, similar to Help Scout's $0.75 and cheaper than Intercom's $0.99), bundled with a modest included allowance that scales by tier (5 to 20 resolutions per user). The most important thing to model before committing is plan-to-plan feature jumps: several reviewers specifically flag noticeable capability gaps between tiers (voice and SMS gated to Pro, screensharing and CSAT gated to Plus), so price out the tier that actually has the features you need rather than assuming Basic covers what the marketing page's headline features imply.

capabilities.note: This is Re:amaze's strongest, most distinctive capability: native Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and Magento integrations that let agents create or edit orders directly inside the chat window, not just view them read-only. The AI Agent's training data includes live product and order information from these platforms, which is a genuinely more commerce-aware foundation than a chatbot trained only on static help-center content.

Email, live chat, SMS/MMS, social media, and voice (Pro+) all land in one inbox, and reviewers consistently name multi-channel communication as a reason they picked Re:amaze. It's a real, working implementation rather than a marketing claim, though voice and some channels are tier-gated.

Trained on FAQ content, response templates, custom context, and live commerce data, with both pre-built and custom chatbot flows available. What's missing from public documentation is any independently verified resolution-rate figure or detailed hallucination-safeguard mechanism — treat vendor claims here with the same skepticism you'd apply to any unaudited AI performance figure.

Two genuine gaps worth flagging directly. There's no confirmed native Salesforce or HubSpot integration — only a built-in 'simple CRM' view of conversation history — and no native multi-language or auto-translation capability; translation runs through a third-party Zapier integration rather than a built-in feature. Teams with either requirement should test these specifically before committing.

Genuinely affordable and transparent relative to enterprise-tier competitors, with a distinctive flat-rate Starter plan for very small, early-stage teams. The tradeoff reviewers flag is real feature jumps between tiers — voice, SMS, screensharing, and CSAT ratings are all gated progressively, so the entry-level price doesn't buy the full feature set shown on the marketing page.

bestFor: Small-to-mid ecommerce brands on Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, or Magento wanting real order-editing capability inside the chat window
Early-stage businesses that want the flat-rate Starter plan's unlimited-team-member structure at a fixed monthly cost
Budget-conscious teams that want ecommerce-focused helpdesk depth without Gorgias's or Gladly's enterprise pricing

verdict: Re:amaze earns a genuinely strong recommendation for exactly the buyer it's built for: a small-to-mid ecommerce team on Shopify or WooCommerce that wants real commerce data — and real order-editing capability, not just a read-only sidebar — inside the same window agents are already answering messages from. That depth, combined with a unified inbox spanning email, chat, SMS, social, and voice, at a price meaningfully below Gorgias's or Gladly's higher tiers, is a genuinely compelling package, and the review record backs it up (4.8/5, though on a comparatively modest 53-review sample). The AI Agent follows the same commerce-aware pattern as the rest of the product, training on live Shopify and WooCommerce data alongside FAQ content — a real, sensible foundation, even though there's no independently audited resolution-rate figure to verify how well it performs against that foundation in practice. Where I'd flag real gaps: there's no confirmed native Salesforce or HubSpot integration, just a lighter built-in 'simple CRM,' and multi-language support isn't native at all — you're routing through Zapier's translation tool rather than getting auto-detection built in. GoDaddy's 2021 acquisition is also worth knowing about, less because it's changed anything specific in the product and more because it means Re:amaze's roadmap now sits inside a much larger company's priorities rather than an independent founder's. My honest read: if you're ecommerce-first, budget-conscious, and don't need deep CRM or multi-language support, Re:amaze is one of the stronger value picks in this category. If either of those gaps matters to your operation, price out a more CRM- or language-complete alternative before committing.
